problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise smooth on $x\in [-1,1]?$

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}4x-3, & x<0 \\ -2x+5, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}\,,\,g(x)={x}^{3}-\sqrt[5]{{x}^{3}},\,h(x)={x}^{3}\sqrt[3]{x}
$$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise continuous on $x\in [0,\infty ).$

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}1,\, & ⌈x⌉\text{ is even} \\ -1,\, & ⌈x⌉\text{ is odd}\end{aligned},\,g(x)=\operatorname{csc}⁡x,\,h(x)=u\,(x-\frac{1}{2})+u\,(x-\frac{1}{4})+u\,(x-\frac{1}{8})+⋯
$$

Note that $u(x)$ is the unit step function, and $⌈x⌉$ is the ceiling function.
feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose $I⊆R.$ A function $f:I\to R$ is piecewise continuous on $I$ if it is piecewise continuous on every closed and bounded subinterval $[a,b]⊂I.$

With that in mind, let's examine each function.

- The function $f(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty ).$ The function has jump discontinuities at $x=0,1,2,…,$ and any closed interval $[a,b]⊂[0,\infty )$ will contain finitely many discontinuities.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14064583/assets/c93cb4cc987ec951236c40a6e961a9eb9f180a594128d4b871692a140faa31e6.png)

- The function $g(x)$ is not piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty ).$ Consider the closed subinterval $x\in [0,2\pi ].$ Notice that the one-sided limits at $x=\pi $ are infinite: 

$$
{lim}_{x\to {\pi }^{-}}g(x)=+\infty ,\,{lim}_{x\to {\pi }^{+}}g(x)=-\infty 
$$

- The function $h(x)$ is not piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty ).$ Consider the closed subinterval $x\in [0,\frac{1}{2}].$ Notice that the function has jump discontinuities at $x=\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{8},…,$ so it has infinitely many discontinuities on this closed interval.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$f$ only."
